name: CEANS
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry CEANS (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/CEANS), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. The catalogue record is empty apart from the id (it comes from the EXPANSE network). CEANS is not a separately recruited cohort: every source describes it as four existing Stockholm cohorts pooled for air-pollution and noise studies (ESCAPE, ELAPSE, EXPANSE), so it is an aggregation. Its members (SDPP, SIXTY/60-year-olds, SALT, SNAC-K) are not in COHO; COHO's TwinGene Study (COHO:0000193) is a sub-study of SALT, and ESCAPE names the member 'SALT/Twin gene', but CEANS used all Stockholm-resident SALT twins, so TwinGene is not listed as a member. Label follows ESCAPE and EXPANSE ('...Noise in Stockholm'); the Swedish multicohort papers call it '...Noise Study', kept as synonyms (with the capitalisation variants). The design reference is Korek et al. 2015 (stroke in four Stockholm cohorts), not read.

name: NBC1967-1976
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry NBC1967-1976 (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/NBC1967-1976), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. The catalogue record is empty: id and name are both 'NBC1967-1976', type 'Cohort study', no country, description or website; it belongs to the EPHOR network. No paper or web page uses the string 'NBC1967-1976'. The likely referent is the Norwegian register-based cohort of everyone born in Norway 1967-1976 used by the National Institute of Occupational Health (STAMI, an EPHOR partner; its other EPHOR entry NWAC is the Norwegian Working Age Cohort, Nor-Work), but no source links the catalogue id to that cohort, and the cohort has no name of its own beyond descriptions ('Norwegian birth cohort of 1967-1976'). The record above is the candidate if the curator accepts the identification; the example quote does not use a name because the papers never name it. Not in COHO under any name. Left unresolved rather than minted on an inference.

name: My purchases cohort
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry CON (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/CON), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. A defined, consenting group of Danish adults whose purchase receipts are collected and linked to registers, run by Statens Serum Institut as part of the Human Exposome Assessment Platform (HEAP); a cohort, not in COHO (the suggested matches Project MinE, Aichi_Con and ESTAMPA are unrelated). The catalogue id and acronym is 'CON'; the cohort's own names are 'My Purchases cohort' (design paper) and 'Mine Indkøb' (website), with the catalogue's local name 'Mine indkøb kohorten'. The only paper found is the design paper, which analyses the cohort's data and serves as the example.

name: Cervical screening cohort
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry CSC (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/CSC), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry LSC (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/LSC), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. TirolGESUND (official title 'TirolGESUND: General Exercise, Smoking Undone, and Nutrition Diet', NCT05678426, ISRCTN15374182; the catalogue's external id 20210420-2560 is the Innsbruck hospital study-register number) is a 2021-2022 single-site intervention study of 156 Tyrolean women (intermittent fasting arm, smoking cessation arm) at the EUTOPS Institute, Hall in Tirol / University of Innsbruck; the 'Lifestyle Atlas' is its multi-omic data portal, so the catalogue's name is the resource, not the study. ACRONYM CLASH: the catalogue id LSC is also the acronym of the Lovelace Smokers Cohort (COHO:0002019); both terms need the editor note. Label choice ('TirolGESUND study', as the preprint calls it) is for the curator; the formal title is given as a synonym. Not minted on 2026-09-25: no paper with a PMID that used the cohort (its example is a preprint); the record above is kept for when one appears.

The country quote is the whole study's; RS-III participants live in the same Ommoord district (PMID:31638273: 'The third cohort includes inhabitants of the municipality of Ommoord, Rotterdam aged >45 years, and was recruited between 2006 and 2008.'). The fourth cohort (RS-IV) is not in this catalogue.

name: DWDC
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry DWDC (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/DWDC), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. IDENTIFICATION IS INFERRED. The example paper does not use the name 'Danish Wood Dust Cohort'; OMega-X is the only text I found with the name. Not in COHO. OMega-X (EPHOR) is not in COHO either; if it is minted as an aggregation, this cohort would be a member with the quote above. Not minted on 2026-09-25: the catalogue record is empty and the identification as the Danish Wood Dust Cohort rests on the id and a network profile; the record above is kept for when one appears.

name: Nordic Children and Adults Born Preterm
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry NORDCAP (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/NORDCAP), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. NORDCAP is register-based (no contact with participants) but has a defined population, all births in Finland 1987–2023 (the catalogue's 1987–2023; one paper describes an earlier extract of births 1987–2016), so it is treated as a cohort, not a registry of resources; the curator may prefer 'not a cohort' if purely register-linked projects are excluded. The project page says NORDCAP also includes a study of the Finnish 1987–1990 birth cohort and has Nordic partners (Sweden, Norway, Denmark), but the catalogue entry and the data described are Finnish only. The paper spells it 'Nordic Children and Adolescents Born Preterm'; kept as a synonym. The Finnish name is the catalogue's local name. Not in COHO; unrelated to the Northern Finland Birth Cohorts (COHO:0000435).

name: Wearable data collection study
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry WDC (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/WDC), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. The HEAP wearable-sensor pilot: D5.4 says 'The wearablesensor cohort in HEAP consists of healthy pregnant and non-pregnant women (N=100)followed up for at least four months' (DataCite text, spaces missing as fetched), under a University of Oulu protocol titled 'Monitoring exposures during pregnancy with a wearable device', with monitoring due to finish in February 2024 (the catalogue gives 2022–2022). The example is the design paper describing the planned study, not a results paper, and it does not use the name WDC; no results paper was found. Parent left empty because the sources disagree: the design paper plans to draw the women from the Finnish HPV vaccination trial cohort, D5.1 from the Finnish Maternity Cohort (MAT, this check), and D5.4 includes non-pregnant women. zenodo.org and heap-exposome.eu (now a hijacked domain) could not be read directly. Could not read: a paper reporting results from the wearable cohort (none found in Europe PMC).

The catalogue id is kept as an acronym alongside the case variant 'Kardiovize'. Could not read: PMID:28812915 full text (design paper; abstract suffices).

note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry BCS 1970 (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/BCS%201970), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. The 1970 British Cohort Study; surprisingly not yet in COHO (only the 1958 British Birth Cohort, COHO:0000207, and the 1946 NSHD, COHO:0001026, are). The catalogue id 'BCS 1970' is kept as an acronym with BCS70. 'British Births Survey' is the name of its 1970 birth sweep ('BCS70 began as the British Births Survey', PMC10244059); '1970 British birth cohort' appears in paper titles (e.g. PMID:41888672, title only). Northern Ireland births were in the birth survey but dropped afterwards, so the country is United Kingdom.

name: EPIC-EUROPE
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry EPIC-EUROPE (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/EPIC-EUROPE), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. The catalogue gives only 'EPIC-EUROPE' with type 'Cohort study': the pan-European EPIC cohort (as opposed to its national parts), i.e. COHO:0000065 'European Prospective Investigation into Cancer'. Add the catalogue id EPIC-EUROPE as an acronym. The term also lacks the cohort's usual full name, 'European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition' ('Within the European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition (EPIC) cohort, 92 immune proteins were measured in baseline blood samples of 406 incident pancreatic cancer cases and 406 sex‐ and age‐matched controls, using the Olink Immuno‐Oncology panel.', https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC13547983/fullTextXML); adding it as a synonym is suggested (the curator may consider it for the label). Not EPIC-InterAct, EPIC-CVD or a national EPIC centre, since nothing in the entry narrows it.

name: SALIA
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry SALIA (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/SALIA), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. The catalogue record has only the acronym. SALIA is the German women's air-pollution cohort from the Ruhr Area and Borken/Dülmen (IUF Düsseldorf); not in COHO under any name. The expansion is written with 'Aging' and 'Ageing' and with varying capitals across papers; the label takes the form in PMID:31137595 ('Study on the influence of Air pollution on Lung function, Inflammation and Ageing, an ongoing cohort study in the state of North Rhine-Westphalia'), the others are synonyms. SALIA also took part in ESCAPE, which is not a parent.

name: Effect of fat quality on blood lipids and immune response
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry NOMA (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/NOMA), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. A University of Oslo randomised dietary fat trial (2012-2014); a trial's participants, so a cohort. The catalogue's name is the project page's title; the study calls itself 'the NoMa study' (also 'The NOMA study' on the page), so NoMa study is the label. Not in COHO; the resembling blood-donor terms are unrelated. Used in LongITools with the Rotterdam Study, which is not a parent. Could not read: PMID:27737722 (design paper, Br J Nutr 2016, closed; requested, not read), PMID:32807640 (closed; requested, not read).

name: HYDRIA
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry HYDRIA (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/HYDRIA), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. The catalogue record has only the acronym. HYDRIA is Greece's 2013–2014 national health and nutrition survey run by the Hellenic Health Foundation: a defined, nationally representative cross-sectional sample, so a cohort. Not in COHO (COHO:0000088 Greece Hellenic Isolated Cohorts and COHO:0000171 THISEAS are different). The first Greece quote is from the paper's methods; the country is given as 'the country' there, so the second quote, which names Greece, may be preferred. The acronym is not expanded in any paper read; the design papers (refs 3–4 of PMID:35334847, a Hellenic Health Foundation report) were not read. A 'Pilot HYDRIA-children' study in children is a separate sample, not this cohort.

name: Fibrefects - Grain fibre modification for gut-mediated health effects
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry FEF (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/FEF), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. The catalogue's FEF is the FIBREFECTS rye-bread crossover trial of the University of Eastern Finland (registered as NCT03550365, whose official title is the label). FIBREFECTS is also the name of the funding project, but the catalogue entry, the trial record and LongITools all use it for this trial, whose participants are a cohort. Country: no read text says in so many words that participants were recruited in Finland; the quote gives the approving ethics committee (Hospital District of Northern Savo, a Finnish region), and the sponsor and all authors are in Finland (Kuopio); the curator may prefer the catalogue's country field or the closed PMID:31136658. The trial id NCT03550365 is offered as an identifier synonym; drop it if COHO does not keep registry ids. Not in COHO. Could not read: PMID:31136658 full text (closed; the Elsevier download came back empty), PMID:28391735 (closed; requested).

name: Piccolipiù
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry Piccolipiù (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/Piccolipiù), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. The catalogue record has only the name. Piccolipiù is the Italian multicentre birth cohort coordinated from Rome (the Local Health Unit Roma E is named as national coordinator); not in COHO. 'Piccolipiù' is a name, not an expansion of anything; since the catalogue id equals the name, the label adds 'birth cohort' so that the id can stand as the acronym synonym without duplicating the label; the curator may prefer the bare 'Piccolipiù' as label. 'Progetto Piccolipiù' is the name of the study's Facebook page given in the protocol. Piccolipiù is in the ATHLETE network in the catalogue, which is not a COHO term.

note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry LISA (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/LISA), matched to the term by name on 2026-09-25; the catalogue's id, acronym and name are added to it.

name: NWAC
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry NWAC (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/NWAC), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. The catalogue gives nothing but the id and that the entry comes from the EPHOR (occupational exposome) network, alongside DWDC, NBC1967-1976 and STREAM. The most likely reading is the Norwegian Working Age Cohort of the National Institute of Occupational Health (STAMI), Oslo: 'The Norwegian Working Age Cohort includes individuals born 1930–1992 and residing in Norway 2000-2010' (PMID:40607777, https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC12414609/fullTextXML), a register-based cohort that seems to overlap with, or be the forerunner of, the Nor-Work cohort (also born 1930–1992, part of the EPHOR mega cohort); NBC1967-1976 would then be the related register cohort of Norwegians born 1967–1976. But no text read expands 'NWAC', so the identity, and whether it is distinct from Nor-Work, cannot be settled. Neither Nor-Work nor a Norwegian working-age cohort is in COHO. Could not read: the EPHOR partner's (STAMI) expansion of NWAC.

name: Foods for weight management
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry ELIPA (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/ELIPA), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. A University of Eastern Finland (Kuopio) satiety and weight-maintenance RCT; its participants are a cohort. The trial calls itself 'Foods for weight management (Elintarvikkeita painonhallintaan)' with acronym ELIPA in its registration; LongITools calls it 'Foods for Weight Maintenance'. None of the open papers that used it says 'ELIPA': they identify it by its registration number, so the example quote names it by ISRCTN 67529475 and that id is offered as a synonym (drop it, and use the closed PMID:37993047 if it names ELIPA, if registry ids are not wanted). Not in COHO. Could not read: PMID:37993047 full text (closed; the Elsevier download came back empty), PMID:37268538 (closed; requested).

name: Cohorte des Consultants des Centres d’Examens de Santé
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry CONSTANCES (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/CONSTANCES), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. CONSTANCES, the large French Inserm/national health insurance adult cohort, is not in COHO under any name (checked CONSTANCES, Constances, Consultants). The cohort's own site writes 'Constances' and its papers 'CONSTANCES'; the label takes the site's form so that the upper-case acronym can be kept as a distinct synonym (the curator may prefer 'CONSTANCES cohort'). The French expansion is given by the catalogue and by LongITools, not by the design paper. The cohort belongs to the EPHOR and LongITools networks and to OMega-X, none of which is a COHO term.

name: GASPII
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry GASPII (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/GASPII), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. The catalogue record has only the acronym. GASPII is the Rome birth cohort (2003–2004), used in ESCAPE and other European birth-cohort pools; not in COHO (COHO:0000199 'GASP' is a Peruvian asthma study, unrelated). The design abstract gives the setting ('two hospital ofRome in the district ofthe Local Health Unit RME', as printed). The Italian form of the name was not found in any text read. The label is the English expansion used in the papers; 'IT-GASPII' is a tag used for it in multi-cohort papers. It is in the EXPANSE network in the catalogue, which is not a COHO term. Could not read: PMID:18326421 full text (Epidemiol Prev, Italian; requested).

name: Kaunas cohort
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry KANC (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/KANC), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. KANC is the Kaunas birth cohort (Lithuania), one of the six birth cohorts that make up HELIX. COHO has HELIX (COHO:0000827) as a cohort (the HELIX subcohort of mother-child pairs drawn from the six cohorts), but not KANC itself; KANC is not a sub-cohort of HELIX (the relation runs the other way), so no parent is given. If HELIX is ever retyped as an aggregation, KANC would be one of its members ('the Kaunas cohort (KANC) in Lithuania', PMC13504928). The design paper calls the cohort the 'HiWATE cohort study'; recruitment is given as 2007–2008 there and 2007–2009 in later papers. The HELIX profile spells it 'Kaunus cohort', a misprint not offered as a synonym.

name: EST-Biobank
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry EST-Biobank (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/EST-Biobank), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. The catalogue records nothing but the id and name EST-Biobank (type cohort study), which can only be the Estonian Biobank of the University of Tartu, COHO:0000064. The term already carries Estonia, EstBB, EGCUT, EBB and EB; it lacks the catalogue id EST-Biobank as an acronym.

name: CELSPAC-YA
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry CELSPAC-YA (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/CELSPAC-YA), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. CELSPAC: Young Adults is the adult follow-up (from March 2019) of the Czech ELSPAC children, run by RECETOX at Masaryk University. The catalogue record gives only the id. The paper calls it a follow-up of the Czech part of ELSPAC, hence isSubCohortOf the ELSPAC entry of this check; the study page (Czech) adds that siblings, partners and anyone born in 1991-1992 may also join ('Stejně tak se do studie mohou přihlásit vrstevníci původních účastníků ELSPAC, tedy kdokoli narozen v letech 1991 a 1992'), so it is not strictly a subset: the curator may prefer to drop the parent. It belongs to the CELSPAC family of RECETOX studies (with CELSPAC: Parents, CELSPAC-TNG, CELSPAC-SPECIMEn, CELSPAC-FIREexpo), which is not a COHO term.

name: Northern Finland Birth Cohort 1986
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry NFBC1986 (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/NFBC1986), matched to the term by name on 2026-09-25; the catalogue's id, acronym and name are added to it.

name: European Longitudinal Study of Pregnancy and Childhood
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry ELSPAC (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/ELSPAC), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. The catalogue entry (Czechia, 1990-2013) is the Czech ELSPAC cohort (ELSPAC-CZ), not the international WHO-initiated ELSPAC, whose seven independent centres included ALSPAC (COHO:0000016), the Isle of Man, Slovakia, Ukraine, Greece and Russia. The Czech team calls its cohort by the full ELSPAC name, which is why that is the label; if the curator wants the label to distinguish it from the international study, 'European Longitudinal Study of Pregnancy and Childhood in the Czech Republic' (the cohort profile's title wording) would do. CELSPAC-YA (this check) is its adult follow-up.

name: Exposome Maps
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry ExposomeMaps (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/ExposomeMaps), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. Exposome Maps (Utrecht University) is a data catalogue of geospatial environmental exposure estimates (air pollution, noise, green space, walkability and so on) across Europe; the catalogue itself types it as a Registry. It has no participants, so it is not a cohort. Its two listed publications are a Science review on the exposome and the EXPANSE project paper (PMID:34414346), neither of which defines a group of people.

name: Perturbateurs Endocriniens: Étude Longitudinale sur les Anomalies de la Grossesse, l’Infertilité et l’Enfance
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry PELAGIE (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/PELAGIE), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. PELAGIE is the INSERM (Rennes) mother-child cohort from Brittany; nothing in COHO resembles it (the suggested COHO:0001679 is an unrelated French myocardial infarction study). The website spells the name with a space before the colon ('Perturbateurs Endocriniens : Étude…') and the acronym as PÉLAGIE; the label follows the catalogue and the EHP paper. The cohort profile (PMID:38760172) would be the better definition source once it is readable. Could not read: PMID:38760172.

name: Generation 21
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry G21 (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/G21), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. Generation XXI (Geração XXI, written Geração 21 on its website) is the Porto birth cohort of the University of Porto's Institute of Public Health; the catalogue's 'Generation 21' is a rendering of that name. None of the suggested COHO terms (GERA, Generation R, Generation Scotland) is the same cohort.

name: Moli-sani Study
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry Moli-sani (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/Moli-sani), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. The Moli-sani Study is the Molise population cohort run by the IRCCS Neuromed; not in COHO under any name. Moli-sani is a name rather than an acronym, but it is the catalogue's id and the website also writes MOLI-SANI, so both go in as acronyms. The Moli-family study listed on the same website is a separate study.

name: Krakow
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry Krakow (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/Krakow), matched to the term by name on 2026-09-25; the catalogue's id, acronym and name are added to it.

name: Central European Longitudinal Study of Parents and Children: The Next Generation
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry CELSPAC-TNG (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/CELSPAC-TNG), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. CELSPAC: TNG is RECETOX's new-generation birth cohort in Brno; the study page (Czech) says it began in 2017 and recruited pregnant women until 2026 ('TNG započala v roce 2017 a nabírala těhotné ženy až do roku 2026'), the catalogue says 2018, and the 2015-2016 recruits were a pilot. It continues the ELSPAC tradition but recruits a new generation, so it is not a sub-cohort of ELSPAC. The papers vary between 'Studies' and 'Study' in the name; the plural is in the ethics statements, the singular is the catalogue's. The acronym TNG is generic and may clash with other studies.

name: CHILDREN HEALTH AND ENVIRONMENT OBSERVATORY
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry CHILDREN FIRST (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/CHILDREN%20FIRST), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. The catalogue entry (Cyprus, 2023-2029, pointing to childrenfirstcy.com) is the Cypriot Children's Health and Environment Observatory, which calls itself 'CHILDREN_FIRST – The Cypriot Children's Health and Environment Observatory' and says it is part of the Mediterranean CHILDREN_FIRST network. The protocol describes CHILDREN_FIRST as one multi-country cohort with sites in Cyprus, Greece and Albania, of which only Cyprus had recruited (Greece had done feasibility work); if the curator prefers one term for the whole multi-country cohort, label it CHILDREN_FIRST and make this a sub-cohort, or widen this definition. The only paper is the protocol, which reports the Cypriot recruitment, so it serves as the example; no results paper was found in Europe PMC. The Greek name comes from the site's about page.

name: Observation of Cardiovascular Risks and Health in Luxembourg
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry ORISCAV-LUX-II (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/ORISCAV-LUX-II), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. The catalogue entry is the second wave (ORISCAV-LUX 2, 2016-2018) of LIH's ORISCAV-LUX study; its name is the whole study's. The second wave followed up the first wave's participants (660 of them) and added new random samples and volunteers (PMID:30717671: 'In 2016, the second wave ORISCAV-LUX study was initiated to follow-up the same baseline sample of participants.'), and later papers treat both waves as one cohort, so one term for the study is proposed, carrying the wave-2 names as acronyms. If the curator wants the second wave as its own term, it would be a sub-cohort of this one. Luxembourg is not in gaz_xrefs.tsv (DBpedia resource Luxembourg); the country also follows from the name. None of the suggested COHO terms is related.

name: Barcelona Life Study Cohort
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry BiSC (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/BiSC), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. BiSC is an ISGlobal-led exposome birth cohort in Barcelona (ERC-funded), with mothers recruited in pregnancy 2018-2021 and children followed postnatally. No COHO term covers it: the suggested matches (Barcelona-1, Triple A Barcelona Study, LIFE studies) are unrelated. 'BiSC Project' is the name the website uses for its project page. The design paper is the IJE cohort profile PMID:38725298, which could replace the website as definition source once its text is available. Could not read: PMID:38725298 full text (cohort profile, requested; not needed for the record).

name: EXOMAIR
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry EXOMAIR (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/EXOMAIR), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. EXOMAIR is a research project, not a group of people. It runs 2024-2026 under ISCIII grant PI23/01032, is coordinated at ISGlobal, and its full title is 'Hacia una Medicina de Precisión: Análisis del Exposoma y Omicas usando Inteligencia Artificial Explicable para estudiar su impacto durante la vida en la Obesidad, Insulino Resistencia y salud metabólica'. The ISGlobal page says it analyses two existing cohorts: 'Se llevarán a cabo enfoques multiómicos y de exposoma a partir de dos cohortes ya existentes: PUBMEP (N=198) e IBEROMICs (N=753).' (https://www.isglobal.org/-/exomair). Both of those cohorts are separate entries of this catalogue (PUBMEP in this batch, IBEROMICS elsewhere). The catalogue's 'hospital cohort' wording describes the data the project uses. It is not a consortium of cohorts either, only one funded project, so it is not an aggregation. Nothing to mint.

name: Puberty and metabolic risk in obese children. Epigenetic alterations and pathophysiological and diagnostic implications
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry PUBMEP (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/PUBMEP), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. PUBMEP is a Spanish multicentre follow-up at puberty of children first studied, before puberty, in GENOBOX. GENOBOX is a separate entry of this catalogue (in another batch), not yet in COHO, so the parent is given as the catalogue id GENOBOX and depends on GENOBOX being minted; drop the parent if it is not. The label is the project title as the University of Granada (UCEENS) gives it, and the catalogue uses the same title. No source expands the acronym, and papers call it 'the PUBMEP study', so the curator may prefer 'PUBMEP study' as the label. The catalogue's 96 children are the epigenetic subsample. The 2022 paper describes 191 who agreed to take part, and ISGlobal gives N=198. No COHO term matches: the suggested Leipzig and other childhood obesity cohorts are different studies. The EXOMAIR project in this batch analyses PUBMEP.

name: Taiwan Elderly Exposome Cohort
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry TEEC (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/TEEC), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. The catalogue describes a real cohort, about 400 older adults in southern Taiwan recruited 2022-2025 with biosamples, but no website, publication or host institution for it could be found, so there is no example study and no source beyond the catalogue. The catalogue says it is 'nested', but not in which parent cohort. One guess is the Taiwan Initiative for Geriatric Epidemiological Research (TIGER, southern Taiwan, collects environmental exposures and metabolomics), but nothing links them, so no parent is given. It is not the same people as any COHO term: Taiwan Biobank, the NCI Taiwan cohort and the Taiwan diabetes studies are unrelated. The draft fields above come from the catalogue alone and could be used to mint it once a publication appears (or as a placeholder, if the curator wants one). Could not read: any publication or website of TEEC, PMID:40737520 full text, to see whether it used TEEC.

name: Study of Secondary Exposures to Pesticides Across Childhood, Adolescence and Adulthood
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry ESPINA (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/ESPINA), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. ESPINA is UCSD's pesticide cohort in Pedro Moncayo, Ecuador: children examined in 2008, with follow-ups in 2016 and 2022 and later ones, and extra participants recruited at the follow-ups. No COHO term covers it: the suggested matches are unrelated. The label is the expansion the 2025 data paper puts in quotation marks. The catalogue's name ('...Across Childhood, Adolescence and Adulthood') and the paper's own variants are given as synonyms. The website mentions an ancillary study, ESPINA-EMCT, that is part of the same cohort. It is not a separate entry.

name: Rome Longitudinal Study
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry ROLS (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/ROLS), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. The Rome Longitudinal Study is a census-based administrative cohort of the whole resident population of Rome, run by the Lazio Department of Epidemiology. It is a defined population followed by record linkage, so it is a cohort. The catalogue describes the enrolment at the 2011 census, followed to 2019. Earlier papers use an enrolment at the 2001 census, with the same study name. The term is defined to cover both, since no source presents them as separately named cohorts. 'RoLS' is the form papers use (e.g. PMID:39032743, 'the Italian Rome Longitudinal Study (RoLS)'), and 'ROLS' is the catalogue's id. No COHO term matches: the suggested longitudinal studies are unrelated.

name: Prevention Cube: data warehouse for detection and evaluation of trends of occupational diseases (Precube)
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry Precube (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/Precube), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. A borderline call. The catalogue and the 2015 paper call Precube a 'data warehouse' of IDEWE's occupational health surveillance records. CHECKM lists data warehouses as not cohorts, but this one covers a defined group of people: all employees of employers affiliated to IDEWE, a Belgian external prevention service, followed with repeated examinations since 1993. The OMega-X cohort profile (PMID:42615545) treats it as one of its 24 occupational cohorts ('Some, however, followed workers from the 1950s (SLFF), 1960s (Danish Styrene cohort, Nor-Work), 1970s (DOC*X, SNOW, SWIP), 1980s (HUNT), or 1990s (ECRHS, GAZEL, PRECUBE, RHINE, the SUS Study) for decades.'). It is therefore given as a cohort. If the curator reads the CHECKM rule strictly it becomes 'not a cohort'. The label 'Prevention Cube' is the expansion only the catalogue gives; papers write PRECUBE. OMega-X (the European Occupational Exposome Mega Cohort Consortium) is not in COHO, so no parent is given, but it would be the aggregation to add Precube to. Could not read: PMID:26503980 full text (closed; not needed for the verdict).

name: Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development Study
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry ABCD study (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/ABCD%20study), matched to the term by name on 2026-09-25; the catalogue's id, acronym and name are added to it.

name: Health, Alcohol and Psychosocial factors In Eastern Europe
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry HAPIEE-CZ (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/HAPIEE-CZ), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. This is the Czech arm of HAPIEE, which COHO already has as COHO:0000265, a single term for all four national cohorts. It is a separately recruited country cohort with its own cohort profile, so it is a new cohort with isSubCohortOf COHO:0000265, as CHECKM anticipates. The catalogue's description is that of the whole HAPIEE study, but its id, country (Czechia) and exposome geocoding point to the Czech cohort. The label is the Czech cohort's own name from the title of its 2026 cohort-profile preprint. The catalogue's name for this entry is the parent's full name, so it is not repeated as a synonym. The parent term's current example is the Siberian (Novosibirsk) branch on EGA, so it is untouched.

name: International Lipid‑Based Nutrient Supplements Project
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry iLiNS DOSE iLiNS DYAD (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/iLiNS%20DOSE%20iLiNS%20DYAD), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. The catalogue's name is that of the umbrella iLiNS Project, a research programme of several trials: DOSE and DYAD-M in Malawi, DYAD-G in Ghana, ZINC in Burkina Faso. Its acronym joins two Malawi trials, iLiNS-DOSE (infants enrolled at 6 months, 2009-2011) and iLiNS-DYAD-M. But its description, dates (2011-2015) and single country describe only iLiNS-DYAD-M, the mother-infant trial. The entry is therefore given as that trial's participants, the group of people it describes, under the full name given in PMID:30426668. The catalogue's umbrella name is kept as a synonym, because the catalogue tags this entry with it, but the curator may drop it if an iLiNS aggregation is ever minted. iLiNS-DOSE is a different set of participants and would be a separate term if wanted; the catalogue does not describe it. Malawi is not in gaz_xrefs.tsv: DBpedia resource Malawi. No COHO term matches (grep for iLiNS, DYAD, lipid-based: nothing). Could not read: PMID:25646337 full text (closed; abstract suffices).

name: New Hampshire Birth Cohort Study
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry NHBCS (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/NHBCS), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. NHBCS is Dartmouth's pregnancy and birth cohort in New Hampshire, begun in 2009 and focused on arsenic and other contaminants in private well water. It has no COHO term: the suggested birth cohorts are unrelated. Its website says it takes part in the NIH Environmental influences on Child Health Outcomes (ECHO) Program ('Our data team and investigators interface with the Environmental Influences on Child Health Outcomes (ECHO) Program to ensure that the scientific aspects of our study are sound.', https://www.protectkidshealth.com/about). ECHO is not in COHO, so no parent is given. The lower-case title form 'New Hampshire birth cohort study' is kept as a synonym under the capitalisation rule. The site says participants now come from New Hampshire and Vermont, but only the United States is asserted.

name: Shanghai Dapuqiao Aging and Cognition Study
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry SDACS (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/SDACS), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. Community cohort of older residents of the Dapuqiao/Dapu neighbourhood of Huangpu, Shanghai, sampled through the city's annual physical examination programme for people 65+, waves 2019, 2022 and 2024. Not in COHO (the suggested Shanghai terms are other studies). The name SDACS and its full name appear only in the catalogue; no paper found in Europe PMC or on the web uses them. The example (PMID:41606232) describes the 2019 wave (same place, programme, dates and the catalogue's exact count of 2287) without naming the study, so its quote identifies the cohort by place and programme, not by name; it gives the age limit as 60+, the catalogue as 65+. The definition rests mainly on the catalogue description.

name: Disease-free Environment And healthy Reproduction for Moms
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry DearMom (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/DearMom), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. Korean prospective cohort of women recruited in early pregnancy for environmental chemical exposure, pregnancy outcome and omics research. Not in COHO (the suggested terms only share words). The full name is known only from the catalogue. The only use found is a 2024 ISEE conference abstract (P104, Eulji University with Soonchunhyang University obstetrics), published in an Environmental Epidemiology supplement that has a PMCID but no PMID, so the example has no PMID; which institution runs the cohort is not stated in any source read. The catalogue also mentions existing cohorts of normal and twin pregnancies used alongside it; those are not part of this term. Not minted on 2026-09-25: no paper with a PMID that used the cohort (its example is a conference abstract); the record above is kept for when one appears.

name: Survey of Health, Ageing and Retirement in Europe
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry SHARE (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/SHARE), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. The pan-European panel survey of people 50+ (SHARE, 2004 onwards, 28 countries including Israel). Not in COHO: the COHO terms matching the name are other things (COHO:0000725 SHARE = Sinai-Helmsley Alliance for Research Excellence, an IBD cohort; COHO:0000604 SHARe = WHI SNP Health Association Resource; COHO:0001011 Genetics of SHARE = Scottish Health Research Register). The acronym SHARE is shared with COHO:0000725, so both terms need the editor note ("The acronym SHARE also denotes ..."); SHARe on COHO:0000604 differs only in case, so a case-insensitive overlap check may also want notes there. Luxembourg, Malta and Slovenia are not in gaz_xrefs.tsv (DBpedia names Luxembourg, Malta, Slovenia given). Country quotes come from SHARE's wave overview pages; Ireland took part in wave 2 only as far as those pages say. The HCAP sister study SHARE-HCAP is not part of this entry.

name: Diagnostic Assessment of Dementia for the Longitudinal Aging Study in India
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry LASI-DAD (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/LASI-DAD), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. The dementia sub-study of the Longitudinal Aging Study in India: LASI respondents 60+ given in-depth cognitive and biomarker assessment, wave 1 2017–2019, wave 2 2022–2024. Not in COHO. Its parent LASI (the nationally representative survey of Indians aged 45+) is in neither COHO nor this check, so no parent is given; if LASI is minted, LASI-DAD isSubCohortOf LASI (quote: "drawing on a subsample of the Longitudinal Aging Study in India (LASI)", https://lasi-dad.org/about/overview). LASI-DAD belongs to the HCAP network of sister studies (HRS-HCAP, ELSA-HCAP, SHARE-HCAP etc.), which could be an aggregation. The synonym with lower-case 'study' is how the website's funding line writes the name; the one without 'of Dementia' is in the wave 2 paper's abstract.

name: Canadian Healthy Infant Longitudinal Development
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry CHILD (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/CHILD), matched to the term by name on 2026-09-25; the catalogue's id, acronym and name are added to it.

name: CHIOMA NWAKANMA
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry CHIOMA (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/CHIOMA), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. Not a cohort. The entry's name and acronym are a person's name, and its description says only that the submitter researches noise, air and water exposures to metals and contaminants in Nigeria and would like to join exposome cohorts for participation and data collection in Africa. No participants, recruitment, design or study name are described: it is a researcher's expression of interest, not a defined group of people. Nothing was searched on the web, since the only identifier is a personal name.

name: Human Early Life Exposome study
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry HELIX (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/HELIX), matched to the term by name on 2026-09-25; the catalogue's id, acronym and name are added to it.

name: Hokkaido Study on Environment and Children’s Health
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry Hokkaido Study (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/Hokkaido%20Study), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. Japanese environmental birth cohort study (Hokkaido University) whose catalogue dates 2002–2012 span both of its recruitment arms. Not in COHO. The study is two separately recruited birth cohorts, the Sapporo cohort (514 mothers, one hospital, 2002–2005) and the Hokkaido cohort (20,926 mothers, 37 clinics/hospitals, 2003–2012), which papers often analyse separately; the curator may want them as sub-cohorts (isSubCohortOf this term; quote: "The Hokkaido Study on Environment and Children’s Health is an ongoing study consisting of two birth cohorts of different population sizes: the Sapporo cohort and the Hokkaido cohort.", PMC8141139). The catalogue's acronym 'Hokkaido Study' is also the study's own short name. The last synonym is the 2017 profile's title as Europe PMC lists it.

name: CA Prostate consortium of India (bioclues.org/capci)
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry CAPCI (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/CAPCI), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. Not a cohort. CAPCI, the CAncer Prostate Consortium of India, is a research consortium of investigators and clinicians, not a collection of cohorts and not a defined group of participants: "The CAncer Prostate Consortium of India (CAPCI) was virtually started in 2016 by a group of researchers and clinicians interested in identifying inherited and somatic risk factors" (https://bioclues.org/capci). Its catalogue description is the aims paragraph of PMID:42246034, whose samples are 49 tumour and BPH tissue samples from two Jaipur hospitals ("The samples were collected from Rukmani Birla Hospital (RBH) and Mahatma Gandhi University of Medical Sciences and Technology (MGUMST) in Jaipur, India, and all patients were identified as native to North or North-west India.", https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC13229647/fullTextXML): a study sample of a sequencing project, with no recruited, described population. The catalogue's acronym field reads 'The CAPCI:'.

name: GINIplus (German Infant Nutritional Intervention plus environmental and genetic influences on allergy development)/LISA (Influence of Lifestyle factors on the development of the Immune System and Allergies) North
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry GINI/LISA North (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/GINI/LISA%20North), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. GINI/LISA North is not separately recruited: it is the Wesel-area participants of two COHO cohorts, GINIplus (COHO:0000708) and LISA (COHO:0000831), pooled and analysed as one unit ("As the GINIplus and LISAplus birth cohorts have nearly identical study designs, data were pooled and are presented per study area (GINI/LISA South and GINI/LISA North).", PMC4112441; ESCAPE: "Individual estimates are presented by cohort except for the German birth cohorts (LISAplus and GINIplus), which had almost identical study designs and parental questionnaires, and are presented as GINI/LISA North (Wesel) and GINI/LISA South (Munich) because separate air pollution models were developed for each area as part of ESCAPE.", PMC3888562). I call it a new cohort because consortia (ESCAPE, EXPANSE) and this catalogue treat it as a named cohort; the alternative is to treat it as an analysis stratum and not mint it. It has two parents: besides COHO:0000708 it is equally isSubCohortOf COHO:0000831 (quote: "LISAplus (Influence of Life-style Factors on the Development of the Immune System and Allergies in Childhood Plus the influence of traffic emissions and genetics) is a population-based prospective birth cohort study of children born during 1997–1999 in Wesel, Munich, Leipzig, and Bad Honnef, Germany", PMC3888562). The label follows the EXPANSE spelling ("Cohorts established in less populated areas (Lifelines, GINIplus/LISA North) had lower exposure levels of IMP and LAN.", PMC12266180); the cohort's own papers write GINI/LISA North, the catalogue id, given as the acronym. The catalogue has no GINI/LISA South entry, but ESCAPE and EXPANSE use one, so a matching term may be wanted. The catalogue's separate GINI and LISA entries are the existing COHO:0000708 and COHO:0000831. Parent not asserted: the group pools children of both GINIplus (COHO:0000708) and LISA, so it is part of neither alone; quote: "GINIplus (German Infant Nutrition Intervention Study Plus environmental and genetic influences on allergy development) is a population-based prospective birth cohort, with a nutritional intervention, of children born during 1995–1998 in Wesel and Munich, Germany" (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC3888562/fullTextXML).

name: The Bangladesh Longitudinal Child-Adolescent Development, Education, and Environment Study (BLADES)
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry BLADES (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/BLADES), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. A new (2022–2025) community-based exposome cohort of children, adolescents and their mothers in Dhaka and Dinajpur, run by SAIST. Not in COHO. Well described on its web page ("BLADES is a community-based longitudinal cohort established by the South Asian Institute for Social Transformation (SAIST) in 2021 across Dhaka and Dinajpur."; "Between 2022 and 2025, the study enrolled 2,455 households, including children under five, school-aged children (0–18 years), and their mothers/caregivers, with annual follow-up."), but no publication using it was found, so there is no example; it cannot be minted as a curated term until one appears. The country is given from the name (Bangladesh); the page names only Dhaka and Dinajpur. Could not read: a paper that used BLADES (none found; the cohort began enrolling in 2022). Not minted on 2026-09-25: no paper that used the cohort yet; the record above is kept for when one appears.

name: Walnuts, Long-Chain Polyunsaturated Fatty Acids, and Adolescent Brain Development
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry WALNUTs (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/WALNUTs), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. A walnut-supplementation randomised trial in about 800 Barcelona schoolchildren (NCT02590848), whose participants the catalogue lists as a cohort; a trial's participants count as a cohort. Not in COHO. The catalogue's name is the protocol paper's title; the trial's own name is the Walnuts Smart Snack Dietary Intervention Trial, abbreviated WALNUTs or WSS in its papers, so that is the label and both are acronyms. Recruitment years 2016–2017 come from the catalogue only; the protocol does not state them in the text read. Later papers pool its baseline data with INMA-Sabadell (INMA is COHO:0000100), which does not make it part of INMA.

name: Mount Sinai EHR
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry Mount Sinai Electronic Health Records (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/Mount%20Sinai%20Electronic%20Health%20Records), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. The catalogue describes this resource as 'The primary clinical data repository for the Mount Sinai Health System (MSHS)', capturing longitudinal patient data across inpatient, outpatient and emergency settings 'via the Mount Sinai Data Warehouse (MSDW)'. It is an electronic health record data warehouse, not a defined group of people recruited or sampled for study, so it is not a cohort. It is not BioMe (COHO:0000424), which is the consented EHR-linked biobank drawn from the same health system, nor any of the other Mount Sinai terms (COHO:0000439, COHO:0001270, COHO:0002091).

name: IBEROMICS
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry IBEROMICS (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/IBEROMICS), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. IBEROMICS is the name of a Spanish grant-funded omics project (ISCIII PI20/00563, PI20/00924, PI20/00988) of the paediatric obesity groups in Granada, Santiago de Compostela, Zaragoza and Córdoba that also run GENOBOX and PUBMEP. The ESPE 2024 abstract treats the IBEROMICS study as its own population of 639 Spanish children aged 8-18 ('an external spanish population'), separate from the 702 GENOBOX children, so it is a cohort distinct from GENOBOX. Its full name (if the acronym expands) was not found, so the label is the acronym the catalogue and the abstract use. Recruiting hospitals are not named in any source read, so the definition says only 'hospital-based' (from the catalogue). It may overlap the PUBMEP children (recruited 2012-2015 and followed into puberty in the same hospitals), which no source confirms. The only example is a conference abstract without a PMID; the curator may prefer to hold the term until a paper appears. Could not read: a PubMed-indexed paper that describes or uses the IBEROMICS population (none found in Europe PMC; the only use found is the ESPE 2024 conference abstract, which has no PMID). Not minted on 2026-09-25: no paper with a PMID that used the cohort, and the group is only thinly described; the record above is kept for when one appears.

name: GENOBOX
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry GENOBOX (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/GENOBOX), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. Not in COHO under any name. GENOBOX is a Spanish multicentre hospital case–control study of childhood obesity run by the CIBEROBN paediatric groups in Santiago de Compostela, Zaragoza and Córdoba (with Granada for laboratory work). No expansion of the acronym was found, so the label is the name the papers use ('GENOBOX study'); 'Genobox' is kept as a case-variant acronym. The catalogue gives 1998-2015 as years, but the ethics approvals are 2010-2017, so no dates are put in the definition. The PUBMEP study (prepubertal children recruited in the same three hospitals in 2012-2015 and followed into puberty) is related but not in this check.

name: Birth Cohort Study of Environmental Exposure  and Childhood Development – PIPAUFRJ Project
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry PIPA (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/PIPA), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. Not in COHO. The catalogue's entry is the main PIPA/UFRJ cohort (2021-2026). The Portuguese name on the project website is 'Projeto Infância e Poluentes Ambientais (PIPA/UFRJ)'; English papers call it 'Rio Birth Cohort Study on Environmental Exposure and Childhood Development – PIPA Project', used as the label (the design paper's title). The pilot (Sept 2017-Aug 2018, 142 women, 135 births) is described by the papers as the PIPA pilot study, a phase of the same project, not a separate cohort, so one term covers both. All papers found so far analyse pilot data; the example is one of them, which names the project. The main cohort's enrolment was planned for all births from 1 July 2020 to 30 June 2021 (design paper); the catalogue gives 2021 as its start. The catalogue name has a double space ('Exposure  and'); it is given both as is and normalised.

name: Programming Research in Obesity, Growth, Environment and Social Stressors
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry PROGRESS (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/PROGRESS), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. Not in COHO (the Mexico City terms COHO:0000520, COHO:0000737, COHO:0000738 are adult samples; the Mexican Biobank is unrelated). The acronym PROGRESS is already a synonym of the uncurated placeholder COHO:0002284 'PSC Resource of Genetic Risk, Environment and Synergy Studies' (a primary sclerosing cholangitis resource), so both terms need the shared-acronym editor note. The catalogue also lists the United States, but only because Mount Sinai (New York) leads the study; all participants were recruited in Mexico City, so only Mexico is given.

name: Infants' Environmental Health (ISA) Study
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry ISA (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/ISA), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. Not in COHO; the only Costa Rican term, COHO:0000078 (Genetic Epidemiology of Asthma in Costa Rica), is unrelated. No other COHO term uses the acronym ISA. The label is the English name the papers use; the Spanish original 'Infantes y Salud Ambiental' is a synonym, as is the curly-apostrophe spelling used in the papers' full texts. The respiratory and maternal outcomes in the definition come from the catalogue record.

name: Algorithmic management at work and Mental Health
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry AM-MENTAL (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/AM-MENTAL), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. The catalogue record is the only source found. It describes a longitudinal survey cohort of working adults in Spain on algorithmic management and mental health, with start year 2026 and end year 2027, so data collection has at most just begun and nothing has been published. If it is a cohort it is not in COHO, and no COHO term uses the acronym AM-MENTAL, but without an example study (and without its host institution or any design detail) it cannot be minted under COHO's rules. The draft record above is from the catalogue alone and should be revisited once the cohort publishes. Could not read: any source other than the catalogue record (project website, protocol or paper) and a study that used the cohort.

name: Multi-Partner Consortium to Expand Dementia Research in Latin America
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry ReDLat (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/ReDLat), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. Not in COHO; none of the suggested consortia match (COHO:0000519 CANDELA is a population-genetics sample, COHO:0001255 GERO is a Santiago population cohort, not a ReDLat site cohort as far as the sources say). Although called a consortium, ReDLat recruits its own participants at its sites under one study-wide protocol and papers call the result 'the ReDLat cohort', so it is typed as a cohort, not an aggregation; the country groups are described as its subcohorts. The label is the full name the cohort uses; 'Multi-partner consortium...' is a case variant used in the design paper's text, and the hyphen variant with U+2010 appears in the Alzheimer's & Dementia paper. 'RedLat' is the spelling in an AAIC 2025 abstract title. The US comparison samples (UCSF) are not asserted as a country because the sources do not say they were recruited as ReDLat participants; the catalogue lists only the six Latin American countries. The catalogue's start year (2014) is earlier than the design paper; no dates are put in the definition. A follow-on phase, ReDLat2 (announced 2026), is not a separate term here. The Latin America and Caribbean Consortium on Dementia (LAC-CD) is a partner network, not a COHO term, so no parent is given.

name: Sustainable plant protection transition: a global health approach
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry SPRINT (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/SPRINT), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. Not in COHO; no COHO term uses the acronym SPRINT (the Systolic Blood Pressure Intervention Trial, also SPRINT, is not in COHO; if it is added later the two need editor notes). SPRINT itself is a research project (environment, plants, animals and humans), but its field study recruited a defined group of about 700 people (farmers, neighbours, consumers) with biological samples, so that group is a cohort. It has no name of its own, so the label is the project's full name as the catalogue gives it; the protocol expands SPRINT as 'Sustainable Plant Protection Transition' and a 2026 paper as 'Sustainable Plant-Protection Transition'. The country quotes for the ten European sites come from the project's case-study pages, which describe the farm areas; the protocol says the human participants were recruited in each case study site ('Farmers, neighbours and consumers are recruited in each CSS'). The Swiss quote names only Canton Bern (the page is titled 'Case Study Switzerland' in the site's map). Slovenia is not in gaz_xrefs.tsv (DBpedia: Slovenia); Czechia is given as Czech_Republic, the name in gaz_xrefs.tsv. The example is the indoor-dust paper, whose samples come from the participating farmer households; a paper on the participants' own samples (PMID:40834561) does not name SPRINT in its abstract and its full text is closed. Could not read: PMID:40834561 full text (the human wristband results of the field-study participants), for a better example quote.

name: Maule Cohort Study
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry MAUCO (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/MAUCO), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. Not in COHO under any name, and no COHO term uses the acronym MAUCO; the Chilean terms in COHO (COHO:0000599 Growth and Obesity Chilean Cohort Study, COHO:0001255 GERO, COHO:0001407 Santiago Longitudinal Study) are different studies. The protocol's title and text call it 'the Maule Cohort (MAUCO)', used as the label; the catalogue's 'Maule Cohort Study' is a synonym. The protocol gives ages 38 to 74; the catalogue says 35-74, so the definition follows the protocol.

name: Survey on Health, Well-Being, and Aging in Colombia
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry SABE (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/SABE), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. SABE Colombia is the Colombian national survey (fieldwork April-September 2015) modelled on the PAHO seven-city SABE study of Latin America and the Caribbean; it is a separate national sample, not an arm of that study, and neither is in COHO, so no parent. The catalogue's start and end year 2025 is wrong (fieldwork 2015). The acronym SABE is also used by other national SABE surveys (SABE Brazil/Sao Paulo, SABE Ecuador, SABE Bogota), none of which is in COHO, so no editor note is needed now. The Spanish name (Encuesta de Salud, Bienestar y Envejecimiento) was not read in a fetched source and is not given.

name: 015National Nutrition Survey (ENSIN in Spanish)
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry ENSIN (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/ENSIN), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. ENSIN is Colombia's national nutrition survey, run by ICBF in three rounds (2005, 2010, 2015), each a fresh cross-sectional sample. The catalogue entry's description is about ENSIN-2015 but its years (2005-2020) cover the series, so the record is for the survey as a whole with the rounds as synonyms; the curator may prefer a term for ENSIN 2015 alone. The catalogue's name '015National Nutrition Survey (ENSIN in Spanish)' is garbled ('2015 National Nutrition Survey'); the label is the survey's own Spanish name as ICBF gives it. The survey's own English name is not fixed in the sources ('National Nutrition Survey', 'National Survey of the Nutritional Situation'), so only the name read is given. Not in COHO.

name: The Cohorts Consortium of Latin America and the Caribbean (CC-LAC)
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry CC-LAC (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/CC-LAC), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. CC-LAC pools individual data from 32+ Latin American and Caribbean cohorts (39 at the 2020 datalock, 13 countries), so it is an aggregation; the catalogue's 'Cohort study' type and years 1990-2010 describe the member cohorts' start dates. Of the member cohorts named in the profile text, only the Baependi Heart Study (COHO:0000623) is in COHO; CESCAS, the 10/66 Study, the Mexican Teachers' Cohort, CRONICAS, the Mexican Health and Aging Study, PREHCO, CRELES and MONICA-Vitoria are not (MONICA-Vitoria is not the WHO MONICA project, COHO:0000118). The numbers inside the quotes are the paper's superscript reference citations as they appear in the fetched text. Cuba, Dominican_Republic and Puerto_Rico are not in gaz_xrefs.tsv. Colombia and other countries appear only in author affiliations; the full country list is in the profile's Figure 1 (an image). COHO:0000519 (CANDELA) is unrelated. Could not read: PMID:32888015 supplementary data pp. 03-06 (list of all pooled cohorts).

name: Ecuador Life
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry ECUAVIDA (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/ECUAVIDA), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. A single-site birth cohort in Quinindé, Ecuador, with 2404 newborns. Not in COHO (the resembling 'Life' terms are unrelated). ECUAVIDA is the study's acronym and 'Ecuador Life' its English name as the profile gives it; no Spanish expansion was found.

name: Banco nacional de tumores terry fox (BNTTF)
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry BNTTF (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/BNTTF), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. Borderline. BNTTF is the tissue and blood biobank of Colombia's Instituto Nacional de Cancerología (INC) in Bogotá. The catalogue's description (from a 2013 congress abstract) does describe a donor population: donors with cancer, without cancer and survivors recruited 2011-2013 with consent, an epidemiological questionnaire and blood and tissue samples, so it counts as a biobank's donors rather than a tumour bank without a described population; the curator may still decide it is a sample repository and mark it not a cohort. Papers use BNTTF-banked samples of INC patients (the example's patients donated between 2007 and 2017). Label is the bank's Spanish name as papers give it; the English forms vary. Not in COHO. Could not read: https://www.cancer.gov.co/portafolio-1/servicios-apoyo/banco-nacional-tumores-terry-fox (blocked, 403).

name: China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry CHARLS (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/CHARLS), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. CHARLS is the well-known Chinese member of the Health and Retirement Study family of ageing surveys; it is not in COHO. The Health and Retirement Study (COHO:0000089) is its US model, not a parent: CHARLS recruits its own sample. The catalogue's description ('Population cohort') adds nothing.

name: Rio de Janeiro Agricultural Health Study
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry ESARJ (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/ESARJ), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. A new agricultural cohort (enrolment from 2024) of the Instituto de Estudos em Saúde Coletiva, UFRJ. It is a cohort and not in COHO; it is unrelated to the US Agricultural Health Study (COHO:0000740) apart from its name. No paper or study page using it was found, so there is no example and the record rests on the catalogue entry alone; it cannot be curated fully until a publication appears. The acronym ESARJ presumably comes from a Portuguese name (Estudo de Saúde Agrícola do Rio de Janeiro?) that was not found in any source, so it is not given. Could not read: any publication or web page of ESARJ (none found); the study's Portuguese name. Not minted on 2026-09-25: no paper or page describes the cohort beyond the catalogue entry; the record above is kept for when one appears.

name: REal-time Assessment of Community Transmission
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry REACT (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/REACT), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. The catalogue entry is the REACT Cohort: the more than 3 million people from Imperial College's REACT-1 (repeated random cross-sectional swab surveys, 19 rounds, May 2020 to March 2022) and REACT-2 (antibody self-test surveys) studies in England who agreed to follow-up. That is a defined group of people, so it is a cohort; REACT-1 and REACT-2 are separately sampled studies that the curator may want as sub-cohorts (isSubCohortOf this term) if a catalogue ever tags them, and their names are not given as synonyms here because they are different samples. The label keeps the study's own capitalisation, which spells out the acronym. Participants were sampled in England only; the country is given as United_Kingdom because England is not in gaz_xrefs.tsv. Not in COHO.

name: 3xG study (Gezondheid, Gemeenten, Geboorten)
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry 3xG (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/3xG), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. 3xG is VITO's birth cohort of 301 children from Dessel, Mol and Retie (near Belgium's nuclear waste sites), with registry follow-up of the municipalities as a whole. Not in COHO. Its samples also contributed to the HBM4EU aligned studies (HBM4EU is not in COHO). The catalogue's end year 2015 is the end of recruitment; children were sampled again in 2019-2020. The capitalisation 3XG, used in HBM4EU papers, is kept as an acronym variant.

name: Growing Up In Hungary, HCSO Hungarian Demographic Research Institute
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry Cohort18 (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/Cohort18), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. Hungary's national birth cohort of about 8,000-9,000 children born 2018/19, run by the HCSO Hungarian Demographic Research Institute (KSH NKI). Not in COHO. The catalogue's name adds the host institute; the cohort's own name is 'Cohort ’18, Growing Up in Hungary' (Hungarian 'Kohorsz ‘18 Magyar Születési Kohorszvizsgálat'), and the apostrophe variants used by the website and papers are kept as distinct acronyms. The quote for Hungary is from the example's abstract, which says the sample is nationwide in Hungary; the country is also in the cohort's name.

name: COMmunity-based Behavior and Attitude survey in Tuvalu
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry COMBAT (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/COMBAT), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. No COHO term matches (no COMBAT or Tuvalu name in coho_names.tsv); the suggested matches are unrelated community studies. COMBAT is a repeated national survey of Tuvaluan adults (convenience sample of households, waves 2020, 2022, 2023) that the catalogue describes as being turned into a longitudinal cohort from 2025. Label is the catalogue's name, which is also the title spelling of the COMBAT paper PMID:38810531; papers alternate between 'survey' and 'Study' and between Behavior and Behaviour, kept as synonyms. Tuvalu is not in gaz_xrefs.tsv; DBpedia resource name Tuvalu. Adolescents were also measured in the 2020/2022 waves (PMID:38810531 mentions adolescent waist circumference), so the definition says adults only where the source does; the curator may widen it.

name: São Paulo Western Region Birth Cohort (ROC)
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry ROC (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/ROC), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. No COHO term matches (only COHO:0001412 Sao Paulo Heart Failure Cohort shares the city). ROC is a population birth cohort of mother-child pairs enrolled at delivery at the University of São Paulo's University Hospital, 2012-2014, in the Butantã-Jaguaré area; its principal investigator is at the Department of Pediatrics, University of São Paulo Medical School. The Portuguese name Região Oeste Coorte is the source of the acronym ROC. The definition comes from the OA paper PMID:33952246 and the catalogue's description; the cohort profile PMID:33049779 is closed and was not readable here, and would be the better definition source. The catalogue's own name carries '(ROC)'; kept as a synonym since a catalogue uses it. Could not read: PMID:33049779.

name: Next Steps
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry Next Steps (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/Next%20Steps), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. No COHO term matches (no Next Steps or LSYPE name in coho_names.tsv; the suggested Lifelines-NEXT and T2D-GENES are unrelated). Next Steps is the CLS cohort formerly called the Longitudinal Study of Young People in England (LSYPE); it is not the separate second cohort LSYPE2 (Our Future), born 2000-01, which should not be merged with it. The catalogue's acronym 'Next Steps' is the label itself, so it is not repeated as an acronym. The cls.ucl.ac.uk page given by the catalogue refused this machine (Cloudflare block), so the design paper is the source. England is not in gaz_xrefs.tsv; United_Kingdom used.

name: Firefighting occupational exposure and early effects on the health of operational forces
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry 4FirHealth (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/4FirHealth), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. 4FirHealth ('Firefighting occupational exposure and early effects on the health of operational forces') is a research project funded by the Portuguese Fundação para a Ciência e a Tecnologia (grant PCIF/SSO/0090/2019, March 2021 to February 2025, REQUIMTE, principal investigator at the Polytechnic of Porto), per https://hera-science.com/project/4firhealth/: 'The project includes the participation of firefighters from different corporations in the Porto metropolitan area in conjunction with agents from the National Emergency and Civil Protection Authority (ANEPC).' Its papers are exposure-assessment studies: air sampling in fire stations and personal air sampling of small ad hoc teams at individual prescribed fires (e.g. 12 firefighters and 5 sappers at two fires), with in vitro toxicity work; no source describes a defined, enrolled group of participants followed as a cohort, and the papers name 4FirHealth only in their funding statements. It is a research project without a defined participant population, so not a cohort. No COHO term matches. If the curator prefers to model the project's firefighter sample anyway, it would be a cohort of firefighters from fire stations of the Porto metropolitan area, Portugal, 2021-2024, with PMID:38922102 as the example.

name: Characterization of the external exposome and its contribution to the clinical respiratory and early biological effects in children: The PROMESA cohort study
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry PROMESA (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/PROMESA), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. No COHO term matches; the suggested HELIX, IDEFICS and Children's Health Study are unrelated (PROMESA reuses the HELIX questionnaire but is a separate cohort). The catalogue's name is the protocol paper's title, kept as a synonym; the cohort calls itself the PROMESA study or PROMESA cohort study, the Spanish acronym glossed in the protocol as 'Origin of particulate matter and its effect on children's health' (the Spanish expansion is not given in any text read). The example is the protocol paper itself, because the only results paper found (PMID:38643821, clearly the same 506 children) does not name PROMESA in its abstract and its full text could not be read; replace it with that paper if its full text names PROMESA. The catalogue gives 2017 as start year; the protocol gives ethics approval in 2018 and fieldwork from July 2021 to January 2024. Could not read: PMID:38643821.

name: Butajira Nutrition, Mental Health, and Pregnancy
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry BUNMAP (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/BUNMAP), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. No COHO term matches (no Butajira or BUNMAP name in coho_names.tsv; the suggested pregnancy and nutrition cohorts are unrelated). BUNMAP is a pregnancy/birth cohort nested in the Butajira HDSS, run by Addis Ababa University's School of Public Health. Start date differs by source: the catalogue says October 2017 to November 2020, PMID:37620778 says the cohort was 'established in 2018' and enrolled March 2018 to December 2019; the definition says 2017-2018. The district is spelt 'Meskanena Mareko' in the paper; the definition uses the usual spelling Meskan and Mareko, which the curator may prefer to align with the source.

name: Young Caregiving Mothers Program (YCMP)
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry Primeiros Laços (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/Primeiros%20Laços), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. No COHO term matches. The catalogue entry is the participants of trial NCT02807818 (80 pregnant adolescents and their children): Primeiros Laços is the Portuguese name of the intervention, which the papers also call the Young Caregiving (or Caring) Mothers Program, YCMP, and now the First Ties Program. A trial's participants are a cohort. The label is the catalogue's acronym and the name the trial papers use; the curator may prefer a label naming the trial (e.g. the ClinicalTrials.gov brief title 'A Home Visiting Program for Pregnant Youth to Promote Early Brain Development'). The trial id NCT02807818 could go in as a cross-reference. The catalogue's type is 'Clinical trial'. The participants live in the same western region of São Paulo as the ROC birth cohort (entry ROC of this check) but were separately recruited through primary care units; no source makes it a subcohort of ROC.

name: Cuenta de Alto Costo
note: Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry CAC (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/CAC), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. Cuenta de Alto Costo (the High-Cost Diseases Office of the Fondo Colombiano de Enfermedades de Alto Costo) is a Colombian health-system body to which insurers and providers must by law report every patient with certain high-cost diseases; it compiles and audits national administrative registries (the National Administrative Cancer Registry, and registries for HIV/AIDS, chronic kidney disease, haemophilia and other coagulopathies, rheumatoid arthritis and more), as the catalogue's own description lists. The entry is the agency and its bundle of mandatory disease registries, not a defined group of people recruited for study, so not a cohort (a health agency / data warehouse). A single registry drawn from it could be a cohort only if a study defines one; papers do analyse 'nationwide administrative registry cohorts' from CAC data (e.g. PMID:40171140, PMID:36742410, from Europe PMC titles), but these are analysis-specific samples, not the catalogue's entry. No COHO term matches; COHO:0001606's synonym 'Colombian Study of Environmental and Heritable Causes of Breast Cancer' is unrelated.
